# Agentic Story Maker

Source: https://github.com/doneman536/agentic_story_maker/blob/main/README.md

# Agentic Story Maker

A modern story generation engine using LangGraph with Dynamic Fan-Out, FastAPI, and FastMCP.

## Features
- **Parallel Generation:** Chapters and images are generated in parallel using LangGraph's dynamic fan-out.
- **Rich Media:** Each chapter includes 2 AI-generated images.
- **PDF Export:** Generates a professional PDF with text and illustrations.
- **GitHub Integration:** Automatically saves stories to the `Agent_Created_Stories` repository if a token is provided.
- **Real-time Updates:** Uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) to stream progress to the client.
- **MCP Server:** Can be used as a Model Context Protocol tool.

## Setup

1. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   uv sync
   ```

2. Configure environment variables in `.env`:
   ```env
   GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_key
   OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_key
   GITHUB_TOKEN=your_github_token (optional)
   ```

## Running the Server

Start the FastAPI server:
```bash
python main.py
```
The server will be available at `http://localhost:8000`.

## API Usage

### Generate a Story
**POST** `/generate-story`
```json
{
  "prompt": "A reclusive toymaker...",
  "max_chapters": 3,
  "github_token": "optional_token"
}
```
Returns a `story_id`.

### Stream Progress
**GET** `/stream/{story_id}`
Connect to this endpoint using an EventSource (SSE) to see real-time progress.

### Download PDF
**GET** `/download/{story_id}`
Download the final PDF once the generation is complete.

---

# Frontend Integration Guide: Agentic Story Maker

Source: https://github.com/doneman536/agentic_story_maker/blob/main/FRONTEND_GUIDE.md

# Frontend Integration Guide: Agentic Story Maker

This guide explains how to build a frontend to interact with the Agentic Story Maker API. The backend uses LangGraph's dynamic fan-out to generate chapters **in parallel**. However, to provide a satisfying user experience, the frontend will use **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** to display progress and make the generation feel like a flowing, sequential narrative.

## 1. API Endpoints Overview

You will interact with three main endpoints on the backend (`http://localhost:8000`):

1.  **`POST /generate-story`**: Starts the generation process.
2.  **`GET /stream/{story_id}`**: An SSE endpoint that streams real-time progress.
3.  **`GET /file/{file_id}`**: Downloads a specific chapter's PDF.

---

## 2. The UX Strategy (Parallel Backend, Sequential Feel)

The backend generates all chapters at the same time. To make this feel sequential to the user:
1.  **Wait for the Plan:** Don't show chapters until the `planned` event arrives.
2.  **Render Placeholders:** Once `planned` is received, immediately render a "Chapter Card" for every chapter (e.g., Chapter 1 to 3).
3.  **Individual Progress:** Give each Chapter Card its own progress indicator (like a spinner or a bar).
4.  **Independent Completion:** As `chapter_completed` events arrive, mark that specific Chapter Card as 100% and reveal its unique PDF download button. (If Chapter 3 finishes before Chapter 1, that's okay—just show Chapter 3's download button).

---

## 3. Basic HTML/Vanilla JS Implementation Example

Here is a complete, single-file HTML example you can use to test the connection and see the logic in action. Save this as `index.html` and open it in your browser.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Agentic Story Maker</title>
    <style>
        body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; max-width: 800px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px; }
        .card { border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 15px; margin-bottom: 10px; border-radius: 8px; }
        .chapter-card { background: #f9f9f9; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
        .status { color: #666; font-style: italic; }
        .download-btn { display: none; padding: 8px 16px; background: #007bff; color: white; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 4px; }
        .download-btn.ready { display: inline-block; }
        #global-status { font-weight: bold; margin-bottom: 20px; color: #007bff; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>

    <h1>📚 Agentic Story Maker</h1>
    
    <div class="card">
        <label>Prompt:</label><br>
        <textarea id="promptInput" rows="3" style="width: 100%;">A reclusive clockmaker discovers his creations come to life at midnight...</textarea><br><br>
        <label>Chapters:</label>
        <input type="number" id="chaptersInput" value="3" min="1" max="10"><br><br>
        <button onclick="startGeneration()">Generate Story</button>
    </div>

    <div id="global-status"></div>
    <div id="chapters-container"></div>

    <script>
        const API_BASE = "http://localhost:8000";
        let expectedChapters = 0;

        async function startGeneration() {
            const prompt = document.getElementById('promptInput').value;
            expectedChapters = parseInt(document.getElementById('chaptersInput').value);
            
            document.getElementById('chapters-container').innerHTML = "";
            document.getElementById('global-status').innerText = "Connecting to engine...";

            try {
                // 1. Send Generation Request
                const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/generate-story`, {
                    method: 'POST',
                    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
                    body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: prompt, max_chapters: expectedChapters })
                });
                
                const data = await response.json();
                
                // 2. Connect to SSE Stream
                listenToStream(data.story_id);

            } catch (error) {
                document.getElementById('global-status').innerText = "Error connecting to backend.";
            }
        }

        function listenToStream(storyId) {
            const eventSource = new EventSource(`${API_BASE}/stream/${storyId}`);

            eventSource.onmessage = function(event) {
                // Handle End of Stream
                if (event.data === "[DONE]") {
                    eventSource.close();
                    document.getElementById('global-status').innerText = "✨ All generation tasks finished!";
                    return;
                }

                // Parse Event Data
                const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
                
                // Handle different event types
                switch(data.event) {
                    case 'started':
                    case 'planning':
                        document.getElementById('global-status').innerText = data.message;
                        break;

                    case 'planned':
                        document.getElementById('global-status').innerText = data.message;
                        createChapterPlaceholders();
                        break;

                    case 'chapter_completed':
                        // A chapter finished in the background! Update its specific card.
                        updateChapterCard(data.chapter_number, data.chapter_title, data.pdf_url);
                        break;

                    case 'finalized':
                        document.getElementById('global-status').innerText = "✅ Process Complete.";
                        break;
                }
            };

            eventSource.onerror = function(error) {
                console.error("SSE Error:", error);
                eventSource.close();
            };
        }

        function createChapterPlaceholders() {
            const container = document.getElementById('chapters-container');
            container.innerHTML = ""; // Clear existing
            
            for (let i = 1; i <= expectedChapters; i++) {
                const card = document.createElement('div');
                card.className = 'card chapter-card';
                card.id = `chapter-card-${i}`;
                card.innerHTML = `
                    <div>
                        <h3 style="margin:0;">Chapter ${i}</h3>
                        <span class="status" id="status-${i}">⏳ Writing and illustrating...</span>
                    </div>
                    <a href="#" class="download-btn" id="download-${i}" target="_blank">Download PDF</a>
                `;
                container.appendChild(card);
            }
        }

        function updateChapterCard(chapterNumber, title, pdfUrl) {
            // Find the card for this specific chapter
            const statusEl = document.getElementById(`status-${chapterNumber}`);
            const downloadBtn = document.getElementById(`download-${chapterNumber}`);
            
            if (statusEl && downloadBtn) {
                statusEl.innerText = `✔️ "${title}"`;
                statusEl.style.color = "green";
                
                downloadBtn.href = `${API_BASE}${pdfUrl}`;
                downloadBtn.classList.add('ready');
            }
        }
    </script>
</body>
</html>
```

## 4. Key Takeaways for React/Next.js Implementations

If you are building this in React, Vue, or Next.js, follow these patterns:

1.  **State Management:** Maintain an array of chapters in your state: `[{ number: 1, status: 'writing', url: null }, ...]`.
2.  **`useEffect` for SSE:** Initialize the `EventSource` inside a `useEffect` hook after you receive the `story_id`. Ensure you return a cleanup function to call `eventSource.close()` if the component unmounts.
3.  **Updating Array State:** When `chapter_completed` arrives, map over your chapter state array and update ONLY the object where `number === data.chapter_number`. This guarantees the UI reflects exactly which chapters finish first, handling the parallel nature of the backend perfectly.

---
